title: Embedded QR Scanning Appliance
summary: A camera-based scanning appliance that connects QR codes to industrial part-information workflows.
problem: Operators need a straightforward way to identify parts and reach their records without navigating a general-purpose computer.
approach: Developed the Python application and PyQt scanning interface.
Integrated OpenCV, a Raspberry Pi camera and GPIO-driven device functions.
Added operator controls for scanning, camera focus and image orientation.
outcome: A dedicated scanning workflow connecting camera input, operator controls and local-network information.
role: Python application development and embedded integration

sections.title: Production records at the workstation
body: Workers scan a product document to open the matching record from a local server, then update the part build sheet as tasks are completed. The terminal connects a camera-based input to the production-information workflow.

sections.title: The operator journey
body: Present the document to the camera, scan the QR code, load the relevant product page and update its information. Touch input is supported, with a keyboard and mouse available as alternatives.
Review and update the build sheet

sections.title: A purpose-built device interface
body: The Python/PyQt application provides scan controls, a main menu, troubleshooting views and camera setup. The project gallery shows these interfaces on the physical terminals and several assembled devices together.

sections.title: Administration over the local network
body: A separate device-control panel provides status, settings and control commands through the network. The demonstration recordings show device development and the remote maintenance workflow.

strength: A production record, opened at the point of work.
highlights: Camera scan to production build sheet
contribution: I developed the Python/PyQt terminal application and embedded integration, connecting camera scanning, operator controls and local-network production records. System design is credited to Hosein AlamShahi.
result: A dedicated scanning workflow connecting camera input, operator controls and local-network information.
decisionNotes: A dedicated Raspberry Pi terminal connects camera input to local production records. Touch controls support the workstation workflow, with keyboard and mouse alternatives and a separate network device-control panel.
validationNotes: Photographs show assembled terminals and application screens. Archival recordings show device development and remote maintenance. No measured scan accuracy, throughput or deployment count is supplied.
